decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar + Serperior for immediate pressure. Incineroar's Fake Out (priority +3) stops Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind/Encore or Basculegion's attack. Serperior's Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert (168-302%), threatens Basculegion (86-156% 2× SE), and pressures Pelipper (59-118%). Contrary + Life Orb turns Leaf Storm into a snowballing +2 SpA boost. Rotom-Wash in back punishes rain with Electric STAB and burns physical attackers; Metagross-Mega cleans late with Tough Claws Bullet Punch and Zen Headbutt. Klefki and Corviknight sit out — Whimsicott's Prankster Encore punishes Klefki's status moves, and Corviknight fears Ampharos-Mega's Electric STAB.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain: Pelipper (Damp Rock), Swampert-Mega, Basculegion (Choice Scarf, Swift Swim), Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Encore). They double-Protected turn 1. Swampert was debuffed to -3 Atk. Basculegion's Last Respects is strong even without rain. Whimsicott has Encore. Game 2: may bring Ampharos-Mega or Primarina; may lead Whimsicott + Basculegion for fast Tailwind. Our Intimidate cycling and Rotom-Wash are key. Serperior OHKOs Swampert. Avoid giving Encore opportunities; consider leading Incineroar + Serperior to pressure early.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper sets Drizzle for Swift Swim Swampert and Basculegion while bringing Tailwind or heavy offenses, with Whimsicott in the back for speed control and utility.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brings Serperior, Metagross-Mega, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash. Rotom-Wash is immune to Ground via Levitate, making Swampert's Earthquake safe against grounding electrics.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out Pelipper stops Tailwind, the opponent's most dangerous turn-1 play. Leaf Storm into Swampert is a guaranteed OHKO if it stays in and doesn't Protect; if it Protects, Contrary gives Serperior +2 SpA anyway. If they switch Swampert to Whimsicott, Leaf Storm chips through Sash and we handle it next turn; if Basculegion comes in, it risks a high-roll OHKO. Stopping Tailwind while pressuring the Swift Swim sweeper is the highest-value line.
Both Pelipper and Swampert protect on turn 1 to waste Fake Out from Incineroar and dodge any potential damage from Serperior while allowing Swampert to Mega Evolve safely.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brings Serperior, Metagross-Mega, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Switch Incineroar to Rotom-Wash (resists Water, immune to Ground via Levitate, takes only 17-38% from Waterfall and 21-50% from Weather Ball). Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert-Mega (145-252%) before or between foe attacks — even if Swampert is faster, Ice Punch only does 41-58% and Serperior still KOs back. Rotom-Wash safely absorbs any attacks aimed at Incineroar's slot. If Swampert Protects, Rotom-Wash is still in a strong position and we preserve Serperior.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Serperior, Rotom-Wash, Metagross. Opponent revealed Pelipper (Damp Rock), Swampert-Mega, and has two of Basculegion/Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos in back. Rain is their win condition; removing Swampert-Mega cripples their offense. Rotom-Wash is our rain check with Levitate and Water resist. Metagross-Mega in back for late-game. Preserve Serperior for cleanup; its Contrary Leaf Storm snowballs.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash dominates Pelipper with 4x Volt Switch and resists both its attacks; no reason to forfeit. Switching Incineroar into the fainted Serperior slot: Incineroar resists Basculegion's Ghost STAB (Last Respects 0.5x) while Metagross is 2x weak to it, and Intimidate cycling neuters Basculegion's physical Wave Crash/Last Respects. Fake Out also provides disruption next turn. Metagross-Mega is better preserved for later after Basculegion is handled.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Serperior, Rotom-Wash, Metagross. Opponent revealed Pelipper (Damp Rock), Swampert-Mega; two of Basculegion/Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos remain. Rain is their win condition. Rotom-Wash is our primary rain check. Incineroar is the Basculegion answer (Ghost resist, Intimidate). Metagross-Mega is weak to Ghost—avoid sending it into potential Basculegion. Preserve Metagross-Mega for late-game cleanup after Basculegion is removed.

decisions.rationale: Swampert-Mega outspeeds both foes under Swift Swim and can KO Serperior with Ice Punch, while Pelipper targets Serperior with Hurricane to pressure it before it moves.
decisions.notebook: Opponent brought Serperior, Metagross-Mega, Incineroar, and Rotom-Wash.

decisions.rationale: Swampert fainted last turn, so we must replace it. Basculegion enters under Rain, threatening massive damage with Swift Swim active, while Pelipper remains on the field.

Volt Switch OHKOs Pelipper through any non-Protect action while Fake Out (+3 priority) flinches Pelipper before it can move. Basculegion attacks in between (Wave Crash into Incineroar triggers Focus Sash at 1 HP; into Rotom-Wash does 26-38% which is safe). After Volt Switch KO, Rotom pivots to Metagross. Result: Pelipper removed, Basculegion Choice-locked, Metagross in safely, rain persists but their setter is gone. Even if Pelipper Protects, we only lose one turn of momentum—but they must also predict perfectly.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Serperior, Rotom-Wash, Metagross. Opponent revealed Pelipper (Damp Rock), Swampert-Mega, Basculegion (Choice Scarf, Swift Swim). One of Whimsicott/Primarina/Ampharos remains. Rain is their win condition. Rotom-Wash is primary rain check. Incineroar answers Basculegion (Ghost resist, Intimidate). Metagross-Mega weak to Ghost—avoid sending into Basculegion until it is locked or removed. Serperior fainted turn 2 after KOing Swampert.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Pelipper sets Tailwind to outspeed any potential Speed control or fast threats like Mega Metagross, while Basculegion hits Incineroar super-effectively with Wave Crash in the rain for a guaranteed KO.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's 4th Pokémon is Metagross-Mega. Basculegion outspeeds everything under Swift Swim + Scarf. Rain is active.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Mega Evolve Metagross and Bullet Punch Whimsicott to break its Focus Sash at +1 priority. Incineroar uses Parting Shot on Basculegion to drop it to -2 Atk, neutering its Wave Crash, then pivots to Rotom-Wash which resists Water and threatens both foes. Bullet Punch goes before Basculegion; even if Whimsicott Tailwinds first (Prankster +1, faster), Sash still breaks. Next turn Mega Metagross finishes 1 HP Whimsicott with priority while Rotom-Wash Volt Switches Basculegion.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Incineroar has 1% HP remaining, and Metagross enters. Basculegion is locked into Wave Crash, which easily KOs Incineroar (foe 2) or heavily damages Metagross. Meanwhile, Whimsicott can use Encore on Incineroar to lock it into Fake Out or Parting Shot (if it tries to move) or use Tailwind / Moonblast. Wait, Incineroar used Fake Out last turn (Turn 3) and Parting Shot/Flare Blitz before; if Incineroar tries to switch or use an attack, Encording Incineroar is incredible. Alternatively, Moonblast into Metagross or Incineroar. But let's check Incineroar: Incineroar used Fake Out on turn 3, so its last move was Fake Out (wait, no, Fake Out can't be used twice in a row normally, but Encording Incineroar forces it to repeat whatever it did or fails if not allowed? Wait, Encore forces the target to repeat its last successful move. Incineroar's last successful move on Turn 3 was Fake Out!). If Incineroar used Fake Out on Turn 3, encording Incineroar forces it to use Fake Out again, which will fail because Fake Out only works on first turn on the field! That's a classic and devastating lock. Meanwhile Basculegion uses Wave Crash into Incineroar to finish it off immediately, or into Metagross. Let's finish off Incineroar with Basculegion Wave Crash into foe 2, and Whimsicott Encodes foe 2 (Incineroar).
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Metagross-Mega, Incineroar (1%), and Rotom-Wash. Basculegion is Choice Scarf Swift Swim.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash (guaranteed KO from 34% but Sash leaves it at 1 HP). Volt Switch into Basculegion does 45.8–86.2%, threatening a KO and forcing respect. Whimsicott's likely Prankster Encore locks Metagross into Bullet Punch — which is fine, as +1 priority lets it finish the 1 HP Whimsicott next turn. Basculegion's Wave Crash is manageable: 26–39% into Rotom-Wash or 37–56% into Metagross, and even a double-target into Metagross (Moonblast 13–20% + Wave Crash) cannot KO. After this turn we have a 2v1 or a heavily damaged Basculegion with a Sash-broken Whimsicott easily picked off.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Basculegion is Choice Scarf Swift Swim Adamant, locked into Wave Crash at -1 Atk. Whimsicott is Prankster Timid with Focus Sash, Encore, Tailwind, Moonblast, Protect. Rain is their win condition; Rotom-Wash is the primary rain check. Metagross-Mega's Bullet Punch is key priority for breaking Sash and picking off weakened foes. After this turn, prioritize eliminating Whimsicott then cleaning Basculegion with Rotom-Wash's Electric moves.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott Protects to stay safe against Metagross and Rotom-Wash. Basculegion is Choice-locked into Wave Crash and hits Metagross-Mega.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion is Choice Scarf Swift Swim. Whimsicott has Prankster Tailwind, Moonblast, Encore, Protect.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch is +1 priority and guaranteed to KO Whimsicott from 34% (50.3-97.8% range, Focus Sash irrelevant below full HP). Whimsicott's only counterplay is a 1/3 consecutive Protect; even if it succeeds, Moonblast does at most 20% to Metagross and we win next turn. Volt Switch is a safe secondary click that finishes if anything unexpected happens.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Basculegion is Choice Scarf Swift Swim Adamant, locked into Wave Crash at -1 Atk. Whimsicott is Prankster Timid with Focus Sash, Encore, Tailwind, Moonblast, Protect. Rain is their win condition; Rotom-Wash is the primary rain check. Metagross-Mega's Bullet Punch is key priority for breaking Sash and picking off weakened foes.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott is alone against Mega Metagross and Rotom-Wash with 34% HP. Moonblast hits Rotom-Wash for neutral/good damage or Metagross for 0.5x, but Moonblast into Rotom-Wash is the only meaningful offensive option. Basculegion is fainted so slot 2 must pass.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 late-game endgame state; Whimsicott left against Mega Metagross and Rotom-Wash.

reflections.summary: We won the series 2-0 by effectively neutralizing the opponent's rain offense. In Game 2, we traded Serperior for their Mega Swampert early, removing their primary rain sweeper, then used Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch and Metagross-Mega's Bullet Punch to pick off Pelipper, Basculegion, and Whimsicott. Intimidate from Incineroar and the chip damage from Fake Out helped control Basculegion's Wave Crash recoil. Our between-game adjustments—bringing Rotom-Wash as a dedicated rain check and preserving Metagross's Bullet Punch for priority—worked perfectly. The team-preview plan was well-suited: we correctly identified rain as their win condition and brought the optimal four. Mega Evolving Metagross was the right choice as our only Mega Stone holder, offering priority and bulk against their squad. Our preparation was solid; the registered six had all the tools needed, and the chosen sets (e.g., Sash Incineroar, Sitrus Rotom) performed exactly as intended.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, consider bringing Corviknight over Serperior if Tailwind control becomes more critical, as Whimsicott's Tailwind could threaten our slower core. However, Serperior’s ability to OHKO Swampert and pressure Basculegion was game-winning here, so only adjust if their team composition changes. Klefki could also be an option if screens are needed against a more aggressive Primarina or Ampharos-Mega, but the current core of Incineroar, Metagross, Rotom, and Serperior proved highly effective.
reflections.notebook: Opponent rain team: Pelipper (Damp Rock), Swampert-Mega, Basculegion (Choice Scarf, Adamant, Swift Swim), Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster, Timid, Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast, Protect). Primarina (Leftovers, Liquid Voice) and Ampharos-Mega (Ampharosite) were not brought in this series but likely carry standard sets. Opponent tends to lead rain core and may double Protect turn 1 to scout. Basculegion locks into Wave Crash, making it vulnerable to Intimidate and recoil. Whimsicott prioritizes Tailwind and Encore disruption. Rotom-Wash is the primary rain check; Volt Switch punishes Pelipper and Basculegion. Serperior's Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert and heavily damages Basculegion. Metagross-Mega's Bullet Punch breaks Sash and revenge kills Whimsicott. Incineroar's Fake Out and Intimidate disrupt their setup. Future prep: maintain similar game plan; consider Corviknight for Tailwind mirror if they bring Whimsicott, but current core is sufficient.

reflections.summary: The series and game were lost (0-2) due to unfavorable matchups against Rotom-Wash and Serperior, which disrupted the Swift Swim rain offense spearheaded by Mega Swampert and Basculegion. Serperior's Contrary Leaf Storm snowballed quickly after trading Swampert on turn 2, and Rotom-Wash's Electric-type moves and Levitate effectively checked both water and ground options.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Whimsicott and alternative special attackers like Primarina or Mega Ampharos earlier or in team selection to deal with Rotom-Wash and counter Grass-types, rather than relying solely on Pelipper and Mega Swampert rain setups.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs Serperior (Contrary/Life Orb), Rotom-Wash (Levitate/Sitrus/Volt Switch), Incineroar, and Mega Metagross. Rotom-Wash and Serperior heavily counter pure rain/ground archetypes; prioritize electric/grass checks and special spread moves in future rematches.
